structure.unit: Sealing of Criminal History Record Information and Court Records

law.catch_line: (Effective July 1, 2026) Disclosure of sealed records; penalty

text.section: It is unlawful for any employee of any department, division, board, bureau, commission, branch, authority, or other agency created by the Commonwealth, or to which the Commonwealth is a party or any political subdivision thereof, having or acquiring access to sealed criminal history record information or a court record, including any records relating to an arrest, charge, or conviction, that was ordered to be sealed pursuant to § 19.2-392.7, 19.2-392.8, 19.2-392.10, 19.2-392.11, 19.2-392.12, or 19.2-392.12:1, or that was sealed without entry of a court order pursuant to § 19.2-392.6:1 or 19.2-392.17, to disclose such record or any information from such record to another person, except in accordance with the purposes set forth in § 19.2-392.13 and pursuant to the rules and regulations adopted pursuant to § 9.1-128 and the procedures adopted pursuant to § 9.1-134.

A clerk of the court shall not be in violation of this section if such clerk informs a person requesting access to a sealed court record that such court record has been sealed and can only be accessed pursuant to a court order.
Any person who knowingly and intentionally violates this section is guilty of a Class 1 misdemeanor.
